News.title: UK & France ‘plan military operation to open Strait of Hormuz’ after Iran war ends as split with Trump becomes clearer
News.content:
A BRITISH and French plan to force open the Strait of Hormuz with minesweepers after Donald Trump’s war in Iran ends will exclude the US.

A rift between the US President and his European allies is deepening after the UK and others refused to join Trump’s revenge blockade of the shipping lane.





Trump weighed up punishing “unhelpful” Nato nations after he blasted the alliance for “failing” over their response to the Iran war – now he is being shut out of post-war plans entirely.

French President Emmanuel Macron said he is planning an international defensive mission without “belligerent” parties – meaning it would exclude the US, Iran and Israel.

Sources close to the plan told the Wall Street Journal that the European ships will not be operating under US military command.

The mission intends to give shipping companies confidence to use the Strait of Hormuz without fear.

PM Sir Keir Starmer and Macron are set to co-host a meeting on Friday with several dozen countries who will discuss how to police the vital shipping lane after the end of the war.

The US will not be at the meeting, officials said, as a rift deepens between Trump and Europe, with fears growing about the US pulling out of Nato altogether.

Germany is set to be involved in the plan.



It comes as Trump told the New York Post that talks between the US and Iran could restart “over next two days” in Islamabad.

The US president first said discussions about more talks were “happening, but, you know, a little bit slow”, before adding that “something could be happening over the next two days” in the Pakistani capital.

Direct talks between the US and Iran ended without a deal on Saturday – JD Vance said that the sticking point was uranium enrichment.

Reports suggest Washington had demanded that Iran stop enriching uranium for five years, but Tehran would only promise a five-year halt.

Trump told The Post today that even two decades would be too short.



He said: “I’ve been saying they can’t have nuclear weapons… so I don’t like the 20 years.”

An American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz began yesterday afternoon, in response to Tehran’s tight grip on the critical oil chokepoint – it applied to any ship entering and exiting Iranian ports.

Starmer and other American allies refused to take part in Trump’s blockade.

Iran had shut the Strait for a second time, despite last week agreeing to a temporary ceasefire deal that was contingent on reopening the waterway.

Trump threatened to sink any ship that dares to defy his blockade, adding that US forces will employ “the same system of kill” used against drug trafficking boats in the Caribbean Sea.



Yet several ships seem to have slipped through the Strait in defiance of the US.

Two of the four ships that passed through are confirmed to have visited Iran – the Liberian-flagged bulk carrier, Christianna, and the Comoros-flagged oil and chemical tanker, Elpis.



The Christianna passed through the strait after Monday’s deadline, sailing from the major Iranian port city of Bandar Imam Khomeini.

The US-sanctioned Elpis headed east across the waterway, departing from the Iranian port of Bushehr.

Both of the other two tankers were linked to Iran ally China – which has directly challenged Trump’s authority over the strait.

The tanker Murlikishan, which is under US sanctions for Iran-related trade, headed west through the strait, coming from Lanshan in China.

Rich Starry – which has been sanctioned by America since 2023 for dealing with Iran – brazenly sailed through the strait in the other direction overnight.



But Rich Starry then u-turned in the Gulf of Oman, appearing to head back towards the Strait of Hormuz, according to tracking data.

It is possible these ships have been broadcasting false position reports – known as “spoofing” – to disguise their locations.

The US military said on Tuesday that no ships made it past its blockade, adding that six merchant ships followed orders to turn back – Rich Starry and the other tankers could have been among them.

The Wall Street Journal reported that 20 commercial ships had passed through the Strait since the start of the US blockade, citing US officials – ships that aren’t visiting Iranian ports are being allowed through the American blockade, but few are daring to make the risky voyage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sources told the paper that the vessels included cargo ships, tankers and container ships, entering and exiting the Persian Gulf.



Some of the ships had removed trackers to avoid attacks from the Iranians.

News.title: Albanian burglary gang who studied floor plans on Rightmove to steal £1m of gems, watches & handbags in spree is jailed
News.content:
AN ALBANIAN burglary gang who used Rightmove to find luxury homes before ransacking them has been jailed.

The six-strong crew carried out their spree across the UK, stealing jewellery, designer handbags and luxury watches worth up to £3million.





Cops said the gang trawled Google and property site Rightmove to study floorplans and pick out their targets.

They then struck under cover of darkness, often climbing into homes through first-floor windows using ladders.



In some cases, terrified homeowners were inside as the thiefs crept through bedrooms hunting for valuables.

Chester Crown Court heard the gang hit 44 properties over a devastating 10-month rampage.

They would ransack rooms, rip sheets from beds to carry loot and even haul away safes packed with valuables.

One raid saw them make off with £238,000 worth of items, while another netted 32 designer watches.



Victims were left traumatised, with some barricading themselves downstairs as intruders moved above them.

One woman told how she and her son hid in fear after hearing noises upstairs, saying they felt “completely exposed and helpless”.

Another victim said her autistic daughter was too scared to return to her bedroom after the break-in.

Judge Patrick Thompson blasted the gang, saying they had been “stealing with no mercy”.

He added: “You have taken their sense of security in their own homes and left them feeling vulnerable and uneasy.”



The court heard the burglars carefully selected properties based on size, wealth and escape routes, sometimes travelling hundreds of miles to strike.

They used hire cars to cover their tracks and targeted homes near major motorways like the M1 and M6.

A “Bonnie and Clyde” romance also unfolded within the gang after ringleader Endrit Nikolli began a relationship with British medical student Jade Tubb.

She compared the pair to the infamous outlaw couple and helped by hiring cars used in the raids.



At her home, cops found stolen handbags linked to the burglaries.

An anniversary card she sent Nikolli read: “To my Clyde from Bonnie.”

Despite the devastation they caused, the gang brazenly bragged about their crimes, sharing snaps of cash, jewellery and stolen safes.



Some even posted pictures flaunting a lavish lifestyle, including trips abroad and luxury cars.

Police eventually cracked the case using DNA evidence, phone data and number plate recognition linking the gang to multiple scenes.

Officers swooped in coordinated raids across the Midlands, seizing hundreds of items including designer handbags and watches.

But much of the haul had already been melted down or sold.

Sidorjan Lleshi was jailed for 10 years and nine months, while Kristian Gropcaj got 10 years.



Krisjian Dedndreaj and George Pepa were each handed nine-year sentences.

Nikolli will be sentenced later this month.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tubb avoided jail but was given a 12-month sentence suspended for two years and ordered to complete 200 hours of community service.

The judge told her to “hang her head in shame” and warned she may have “thrown away” her medical career.

News.title: Moment animal rights activist steals lobster from restaurant’s tank before pushing past staff to put animal in harbour
News.content:
THIS is the moment an animal rights activist steals a lobster from a restaurant’s tanks and takes it to the harbour to set it free.

CCTV footage shows Emma Smart, 47, fending off two employees and taking a live crustacean, which the restaurant kept for educational purposes.





Smart, in a rainbow jumper, can be seen strolling into Catch in Weymouth, Dorset, and hastening towards the tank.

A member of staff spots the marine biologist and tries to block her from plunging her hand into the crustacean tank.

After a struggle, the mum-of-two manages to grab a lobster and strides towards the door while the member of staff tries to stop her by holding onto her arm.



An outdoor camera captures Smart charging the final few yards from the restaurant to the harbour with the crustacean in hand while the same employee is pulled after her.

A second member of staff runs after the eco-activist but the lobster liberation cannot be stopped and Smart drops her catch into the sea

The crustacean has not been seen since its release on April 10 and its survival remains unknown.

The lobster belonged to the restaurant’s owner Anthony Cooper for two-and-a-half years and was not for sale but used for “educational” purposes when children visited.



Smart, who lives in West Wales, admitted to one count of causing criminal damage to a lobster at Bournemouth Crown Court.

Defending, Kitan Ososami said Ms Smart “acted on impulse. She cares very deeply about animals and marine welfare and this was the driving factor behind her committing this offence.”

She was given a conditional discharge lasting for eight months and a three year restraining order banning her from going within 10 metres of the restaurant or approaching staff or guests.

Her Honour Judge Susan Evans said: “The lobster was not there for consumption. It was there for educational purposes.

“You were determined to take it from the tank and you placed it in the harbour.



“It was a deeply misguided thing to have done.

“It was not a good thing for the lobster at all and whether or not it survived, we don’t know.”

Smart had previously appeared in court over an incident at the Catch in 2022 when she tried to barge her way in to speak to veteran broadcaster and naturalist Sir David Attenborough.

She urged Sir David to support climate activists in prison and refused to leave when asked, shouting up the stairs where the broadcaster was eating with his production team.

Smart was dragged out by two police officers and the restaurant owner but continued to her tirade outside.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She was issued with a section 35 dispersal order and then arrested for failing to comply with it.

Smart was later cleared of the charge when a judge ruled she had not been given enough time to comply with the order.

News.title: Trump claims soda is good for him because it kills cancer cells & jokes that Fanta is freshly squeezed, Dr Oz reveals
News.content:
PRESIDENT Donald Trump has claimed that Diet Coke is healthy and can help fight cancer – as well as joking that Fanta is freshly squeezed, according to Dr Oz.

The president’s bonkers medical theory was revealed by Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr Mehmet Oz, as he chatted on a podcast with Donald Trump Jr.





Oz recalled a meeting with President Trump and Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Junior, saying: “Bobby and I usually go to the meetings together…

“Then comes the diet soda pops, which your dad argues that diet soda is good for him because it kills grass [when] it’s poured on grass, so therefore, it must kill cancer cells inside the body.”

There is no evidence that Diet Coke or other fizzy sodas kill cancer – in fact, the medical community agrees that the drinks are unhealthy, with some research linking the drinks to weight gain.



Oz explained how Trump shows off his candy stash and summons a glass of diet soda by pressing a red button.

The doctor has campaigned with Kennedy Jr on reducing processed foods in the diets of the American people – but they don’t seem to have converted their boss.

Oz told Trump Jr of his dad’s comments about Fanta, saying: “We were on Air Force One the other day, and I walk in there because he wants to talk about something, and he’s got an orange soft drink on his desk.

“I said, ‘Are you kidding me.’



“So he starts to sheepishly grin.

“He goes, ‘You know, this stuff is good for me, it kills cancer cells.’

“And then he tells me, ‘It’s fresh squeezed, so how bad could it be for you?’”

Despite the strange soda theory, the pair agreed the 79-year-old president was “in perfect health”.

Trump has a well-documented love of fast food – in 2017 a book revealed that he wolfed down McDonald’s, pizza and Kentucky Fried Chicken as he jetted around the US on the campaign trail.



“On Trump Force One there were four major food groups: McDonald’s, Kentucky Fried Chicken, pizza and Diet Coke”, authors Corey Lewandowski and David Bossie wrote.

His typical order was: “Two Big Macs, two Fillet-O-Fish, and a chocolate malted.”

Is diet soda healthy? PRESIDENT Donald Trump has reportedly claimed that diet sodas are healthy because they "kill cancer cells inside the body”. There is no evidence for this – in fact medical experts generally agree that the fizzy drinks are unhealthy. While diet sodas have less sugar than their full fat alternatives, and can be helpful to reduce sugar intake, they do not provide nutritional value. Some research suggests the drinks are linked to weight gain. And fizzy sodas can cause tooth decay regardless of sugar content, because of their high acidity. Cancer Research UK has said the sweeteners found in these drinks do not cause cancer, but that doesn’t mean they are at all helpful in treating the disease.

And the US President tried out life as a McDonald’s worker while campaigning in the Philadelphia suburbs – an important area in the swing state – in 2024.

Trump is also known for his unusual medical theories – in 2020, he suggested injecting patients with ‘disinfectant’ and blasting them with UV light to treat coronavirus.

He told a press conference: “I see the disinfectant, where it knocks it out in a minute, one minute, and – is there a way we can do something like that?



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“By injection inside or almost a cleaning. As you can see, it gets in the lungs, and it does a tremendous number on the lungs.”

Disinfectants are extremely harmful to humans.

News.title: King Charles saved from dreaded Oval Office showdown with Trump as pair to have tea behind closed doors
News.content:
KING Charles will be saved from a dreaded Oval Office showdown when he meets Donald Trump in Washington DC with UK and US relations at an all-time low.

President Trump will speak to Charles in private during his four-day State Visit with efforts made to keep off-the-cuff conversations between the two off the air.





It comes after a string of high-profile world leaders including Ukraine‘s Volodymyr Zelensky, Japanese PM, German Chancellor and Saudi Crown Prince have all been embarrassed during toe-curling on-camera face-offs when sat with Trump in the Oval Office.

Instead, the King and Trump will have a private tea hours after arrival followed the next day by a one-on-one without journalists or a film crews in The White House

But the King will publicly speak of “challenges” the US and UK face when he delivers his scripted speech to 535 lawmakers in Congress which will also be broadcast on American telly.

And both Trump and Charles will read prepared speeches at a glittering White House State Dinner.

Sources insist the President and King will also be seen together during arrivals and departures at The White House and during a formal ceremonial military review.

Unveiling fresh details, Buckingham Palace insisted the visit will celebrate the 250th anniversary of US independence and links between the two nations.

The State Visit later this month comes as Trump has blasted PM Starmer’s response to the Iran crisis and said he was “not happy with the UK” and added “this is not Winston Churchill we’re dealing with.”

Despite calls for Charles and Camilla to meet Jeffrey Epstein victims amid the arrest of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor the palace reiterated earlier guidance that meetings cannot take place while any legal action is ongoing.



Charles and Camilla will also meet heroes, survivors and victims families of 9/11 in New York and join a ‘block party’ to celebrate America’s 250th birthday.

A Buckingham Palace spokesperson insisted the visit was a chance to “reaffirm” and “renew” the Special Relationship and address “challenges together”.

The palace said: “This is celebrating a partnership between two nations and two peoples.

“It is a relationship that has survived many presidencies and of course many reigns, and will no doubt continue to do so long into the future.”

Charles and Camilla arrive on Monday April 27, and have private tea with Trump and Melania before attending a Garden Party celebrating the connections between the two nations.



The following day they will be received at The White House with a full military review.

Charles will then have an off-camera bilat, or one-to-one, with the President, in The Oval Office.

Last April, Zelensky’s meeting with Trump in the same room descended into a slanging match.

The President said: “Don’t tell us what we’re going to feel. You’re in no position to dictate that.”

He added: “You don’t have the cards right now. You’re gambling with millions of lives.”



While Vice President JD Vance said to the Ukrainian leader “just say thank you”.

A member of the US media pack during the so-called press ‘spray’ blasted Zelensky for not wearing a suit.

Hosting German Chancellor Friedrich Merz last June, Trump suggested the anniversary of D-Day was “not a pleasant day for you.”

Merz diplomatically replied: “In the long run, Mr. President, this was the liberation of my country from Nazi dictatorship.”

In November, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was subjected to questions about his involvement in the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi during his Oval Office meeting with Trump.



Last month, Trump made a joke about the Pearl Harbor raid by the Japanese on the US in 1941.

Sitting opposite Japan‘s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in the Oval Office, Trump responded after being asked by a journalist why he had not warned allies ahead of initial strikes against Iran in February.

He said: “Who knows better about surprise than Japan? Why didn’t you tell me about Pearl Harbor?”



The US leader has been vicious in his attacks against Starmer and the PM’s response to Iran.

But he has been consistently warm towards the King and last September at Windsor Castle called the King a “very, very special man”.

Later on the trip’s second day, Charles will become the second monarch after Queen Elizabeth II in 1991 to address a joint meeting of Congress.

A palace spokesman said: “Marking a key moment in the visit, the King, accompanied by the Queen, will deliver an address to a joint meeting of Congress in which His Majesty will recognise the challenges that our countries face.”

At a State Dinner both Trump and Charles will make toasts.



The royals will then head to New York for events which will “reflect the economic relationship” between UK and US and the “strong cultural ties”.

A palace spokesman said: “In recognition of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks later this year – a poignant moment in our recent shared history – Their Majesties will commemorate those who lost their lives on 9/11 and meet serving first responders as well as the families of victims.”

In the Big Apple, they will also visit an urban farming project, a literature event marking Winnie the Pooh’s 100th birthday, and a King’s Trust reception.

On their final day in the US they will lay a wreath and flowers to fallen UK and US war heroes, visit indigenous communities and attend a 250th independence anniversary street party.

A Buckingham Palace spokesman said: “The visit will mark, with the American people, the 250th anniversary of the US Declaration of Independence.



“It will also be an opportunity to mark the shared history of the two nations, and the breadth of the economic, security and cultural relationship that has developed since then, as well as the deep people-to-people links which unite our communities.

“Their Majesties will undertake engagements reflecting the relationship, engaging with communities across America.

“The visit also recognises the challenges the United Kingdom, the United States, and our Allies face across the world.

“This visit is a moment to reaffirm and renew our bilateral ties as we address those challenges together, in the UK’s national interest.”

A Foreign and Commonwealth Office spokesman said: “This historic state visit will commemorate the United States‘ 250th anniversary and demonstrate the very best of the UK US relationship that is central to our shared prosperity and security and our history.



“The milestone celebrations provide us an opportunity to reflect on the development of our relationship over 250 years into what is the closest of friendships.”

They added: “Their Majesties’ visit to the United States will strengthen the UK’s long-lasting ties of friendship with the American people for another 250 years and longer.”

The trip comes just seven months after Trump’s ‘truly historic’ and “unprecedented” UK State Visit at Windsor Castle.

But since then, Trump and Starmer have faced public disagreements over the conflict in Iran.

The King and Queen have both been hailed for skilled soft power during State Visits during their reign, to France, Germany and Italy.



Ahead of the US State Visit, an FCDO spokesman said: “So yes, we are close allies, we do disagree on things, but that doesn’t distract from the value that both sides get from this relationship and have done over many decades.”

Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna has led calls for Charles and Camilla, who campaigns against sexual violence, to meet victims and survivors of Jeffrey Epstein.

There are no plans for any public private meetings, although it is expected that victims of sexual abuse unconnected to Epstein are likely at some of the State Visit engagements and the programme is likely to engage with domestic abuse organisations during the trip.

A Buckingham Palace source said: “There is no deviation from the guidance that we’ve previously issued, that it will not be possible during this State Visit for a meeting to take place of the kind that has been suggested.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We fully understand and appreciate the survivors’ position, but can only reiterate that our position is clear that anything that could potentially impact on ongoing police inquiries and assessments and any potential legal action that could result from that would be to the detriment of the survivors themselves in their pursuit of justice.”



Following the four-day US State Visit, Charles will travel without Camilla to Bermuda which is a British Overseas Territory for a two-day official visit.

News.title: Family of US influencer, 31, who died on Africa trip with fiancé demands answers as her lover ‘snubs their calls’
News.content:
THE distraught family of an American influencer who died during her “dream” trip to Africa has demanded answers from authorities.

They are also keen to speak with the fiancé of Ashlee Jenae, 31, whose real name was Ashly Robinson.





The content creator’s sudden death was announced on April 12, just a week after her 31st birthday while on holiday.

Her family said the lifestyle influencer died during “what should have been one of the happiest trips of her life, a birthday celebration in Zanzibar, Africa.”

Her death was “suspicious,” they added, while describing themselves as “completely devastated.”

“Surrounded by beauty, love, and wildlife, she became engaged during a safari, an unforgettable moment that marked the start of a future she was so excited to build,” her family posted on Instagram on April 12.



“She and her fiancé, Joe McCann, were staying in a luxury villa at the Zuri Zanzibar, continuing what we believed was her dream trip.

“But just days later, that dream turned into our family’s worst nightmare. Ashly was found unconscious in her villa and was rushed to a local hospital, where her death was confirmed hours later.”

They told TMZ that it was difficult to get answers as her fiancé was not currently communicating with them.

Joe McCann is a founder of cryptocurrency fund Asymmetric Financial.



The U.S. Sun was unable to contact him for comment on the woman’s death.

Ashly’s family has also sought CCTV footage from the hotel – so far to no avail.

“The suddenness, the unanswered questions, and the distance from home have made this tragedy even more overwhelming for our family,” her relatives added on Instagram.



“She was loved. She was not just going to be discarded and forgotten about,” her mother, Yolanda Denise Endres, told ABC affiliate WPVI.

She told the broadcaster that the South Jersey woman’s death occurred when Ashly “was starting the next chapter of her life.”

Her daughter was found dead four days after she had called her mom to say that she and her fiancé had argued and were staying in separate rooms at the hotel.

A hospital gave her cause of death as cerebral hypoxia by strangulation and suffocation.

“She’s never done anything that would ever ever lead me to believe that she would do something to harm herself like that. She was happy,” Endres added.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The U.S. Sun has contacted the US Embassy in Tanzania for comment.

News.title: Iran to execute its first female protester as lethal crackdown continues months after protests despite Trump war
News.content:
RUTHLESS REGIME Iran to execute its first female protester as lethal crackdown continues months after protests despite Trump war

IRAN is set to execute its first female protester as the Islamic Republic’s brutal crackdown on anti-regime demonstrations in January continues.

The country has already hanged seven people in connection with the protests which left thousands dead and many more in prison.





Four more people were sentenced to death today by a Tehran Revolutionary Court presided over by notorious judge Imam Afshari.

Among them were Bita Hemmati and her husband Mohammadreza Majidi-Asl.

Two other men were sentenced to death, Behrouz Zamaninejad and Kourosh Zamaninejad, who lived in the building as the married couple.

According to the US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency and the Abdorrahman Boroumand Center, all four were convicted of carrying out actions on behalf of the United States.

They were initially accused of throwing concrete blocks from their residential building onto state security forces below.

While it is not clear when the verdict was issued, it is widely believed Hemmati is the first woman to be sentenced to death over the protests.

The Abdorrahman Boroumand Center said it also believed Hemmati was the woman who appeared in a video broadcast on state television in January.

In the footage, the unnamed woman was personally interrogated by judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei.



“The recording and broadcasting of forced confessions from defendants in an opaque process… constitutes a blatant violation of the defendant’s right,” the group said.

These and other human rights groups have accused the regime of using the death penalty as tool to strike fear into the hearts of the Iranian people.

There are also fears that the use of capital punishment will only increase in the aftermath of its bitter conflict against the United States and Israel.

This comes as reports suggest the death toll from protests has now risen past 33,000.

Previous estimates had suggested between 16,500 and 18,000 people had been killed amid two weeks of unrest.



But new research suggests the real tally is at around 33,100.

Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHR) and Paris-based Together Against the Death Penalty (ECPM) published an annual report on Monday, revealing at least 1,630 people were executed in 2025.

This figure is thought to include 48 women – of which 21 were executed for the murder of their partners.

The report also said the figure was by far the highest since the IHR started keeping track in 2008.

To make matters worse, several hundred more are facing charges that could see them executed.



“Dozens of individuals arrested during the January 2026 protests have been sentenced to death following grossly unfair, fast-tracked trials conducted without due process, access to independent counsel and reliance on torture-tainted forced ‘confessions’ as evidence,” said New York-based Centre for Human Rights in Iran.

Earlier this month, Iran hanged an 18-year-old musician in the Ghezel Hesar prison.

This was despite hopes Amirhossein Hatami would be spared because of his age.

Hatami was convicted of “Moharebeh” – meaning “Enmity Against God” – and sentenced to death on February 7.

Days later, Mohammadamin Biglari, 19, and Shahin Vahedparast Kalour, 30, were executed at Ghezel Hesar Prison.



The young men were seized during a protest in January and accused of arson over a fire at the base of the feared Basij paramilitary base.

In February, 19-year-old Saleh Mohammadi was sentenced to death for murder after allegedly being tortured into confessing the crime.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nima Far, a human rights activist and Iranian combat athlete, told Fox News: “His execution was a blatant political murder, part of the Islamic Republic’s pattern of targeting athletes to crush dissent and terrorise society.”

Mohammadi competed in the 2024 International Saytiev Cup in Russia, winning bronze.

News.title: Inside petrol price protests paralysing Ireland as fuming drivers gridlock country over costs – so will Britain be next?
News.content:
HAULIER Michael Horan fears his century-old family business may be reaching the end of the road.

Since the Iran war, his diesel bill to run five lorries delivering grain across Ireland — which need 15,000 litres of fuel a month — has rocketed by over £6,500.





“We’re barely surviving,” the dad-of-two tells me.

“We’re on the floor.

“There’s no future in this business.”

Shaking his head, he blames crippling tax rates — including green levies — which make up around half the cost of a tank of diesel.



It’s why the Irishman has joined hundreds of other hauliers, farmers, coach drivers, contractors and motorists on protests that have paralysed Ireland in the last week.

Angry demonstrators blockaded the Whitegate Oil Refinery in Cork, picketed ports and caused tailbacks on motorways with tractor convoys.

Holidaymakers were forced to trudge down the M50’s hard shoulder lugging their suitcases after protesters blocked the motorway leading to Dublin Airport.

O’Connell Street in the heart of the capital was closed by HGVs and tractors bearing placards No Fuel, No Food and Can’t Afford to Move.



Farming contractor Christopher Duffy told fuel protesters in Dublin: “We have the country by the balls.”

A panicked Irish government called out the army before announcing tax cuts on petrol and diesel.

Now British farmers are threatening fuel protests unless Chancellor Rachel Reeves slashes taxes.

William Taylor, co-ordinator of the UK’s Farmers For Action, raised the spectre of the 2000 British fuel protests when farmers blockaded six of the country’s largest refineries.

The farmer said: “Farmers For Action was born out of the fuel strike of 2000, where the UK was brought to a standstill for five days until Government listened.



“A lot was learnt.”

Howard Cox, founder of lobby group FairFuelUK, said British demos won’t target fuel depots or block roads.

Reform’s 2024 candidate for London mayor added: “I am in discussions to hold fuel protests across the UK.

“They will be peaceful demonstrations by farmers, small businesses, taxi drivers and motorists who are being punished by Rachel Reeves’ inaction to help motorists during a cost-of-living crisis.”

The shock waves from the Iran war are now reverberating 3,700 miles away from the dust-bowl Middle East amid the emerald-green fields of County Kildare.



In this idyllic patchwork of thoroughbred stud paddocks and cattle meadows, many have been radicalised by what they say is a fight for their livelihoods.

Farmer and agricultural contractor John Dallon, 61, has been one of the most prominent voices in the protests which began on April 7.

John, who farms beef cattle in Crookstown, County Kildare, told me: “We don’t know where the diesel price is going to finish up.



“It is escalating and escalating.

“The cost of living is going through the roof.

“It’s affecting people from the farming sector to the haulage sector, the building industry and the bus companies bringing the children to school.

“The people of this country are crying out to the government to save our economy.”

The Irish protests have been likened to the gilets jaunes (yellow vests) grassroots fuel demonstrations which rocked France in 2018.



Fourth-generation beef farmer John says of his new-found campaigning zeal: “I’m not a political man but I’ve become so angry at the way our government is going.

“They’re disconnected from ordinary people.”

He also raised the spectre of the demos migrating across the Irish Sea as English farmers are “under atrocious pressure”.

And he added that the British government needs to remember that “farmers are the people who put food on the table three times a day”.

The global fuel crisis shows little sign of abating.



On Monday the US announced it would blockade Iranian ports after the mullahs closed the Strait of Hormuz to most shipping.

Oil has soared to over $100 a barrel and prices at the fuel pump have rocketed across the world.

Rural Ireland — which relies on diesel for its tractors and lorries as well as kerosene to heat many remote homes — began to buckle as diesel prices rose by more than 20 per cent.



Any rise in prices means more tax revenue for the Irish exchequer.

Yesterday at a garage on the N7 motorway, unleaded petrol was priced at almost €2 (£1.74) per litre with premium diesel just under €2.28 (£1.98).

Farmers and lorry drivers recently began to organise to protect their livelihoods.

WhatsApp groups and social media turned it into a nationwide protest.

Their demands included a cap on fuel prices at around €1.85 (£1.60) for regular diesel and €1.10 (96p) for kerosene home heating oil, the axing of carbon fuel tax plus energy credits for households and businesses.



A poll by ⁠the Sunday Independent newspaper showed that 56 per cent of voters back the protesters.

Convoys of slow-moving tractors led to motorway gridlock, and the country’s only major fuel depots — in Limerick and Galway — were blockaded.

For five days, farmers, hauliers and taxi drivers blocked Cork’s Whitegate refinery which produces all of Ireland’s petrol and diesel.

Panic buying spread like wildfire, and 600 out of Ireland’s 1,500 petrol stations ran dry.

Irish Finance Minister Simon Harris called it a “very dangerous moment”, while Prime Minister Micheal Martin said the blockade was “damaging Ireland’s economy and society”.



The leader of the centre-right Fianna Fail party added that “self- appointed” groups do not have a right to “close down the country”.

Ireland’s government was forced to act, and on Saturday police — backed by army engineers with heavy-lifting trucks — moved to clear the Whitehaven refinery blockade.

Tensions flared as officers used pepper spray on protesters with video footage showing at least one demonstrator being dragged from a tractor.



Cops said they broke up the blockade to protect “emergency public services, including ambulance and fire services” from fuel shortages.

In the early hours of Sunday morning, riot police and mounted officers broke up the protest in O’Connell Street as a helicopter hovered above.

Farmer John Dallon, who was present, told me: “I thought I was in Beirut.

“A swarm of police came in.

“Everyone was frightened.



“I’ve never seen anything like it.

“You’re allowed under constitutional right to have peaceful protests.”

Other blockades across the country were also broken up, and on Sunday the Irish government announced a £440million package of measures to tackle the crisis.

It includes tax cuts of around 9p to both petrol and diesel until the end of July, delaying carbon tax increases until October and millions in subsidy for the worst-hit industries.

Yet the convoy go-slows continued to cause traffic jams on a number of Irish main roads on Monday, with tractor protests spreading to Northern Ireland on yesterday.



In the coffee shop at a Texaco garage in Crookstown I met local haulier Kevin Doody, 48, who says his latest fuel bill is rising by more than the government’s tax cut.

The dad-of-three from Grangecon, County Wicklow, whose 13 trucks and 17 staff ferry refrigerated beef across Ireland, said: “The tax break has already disappeared.

“They need to get rid of the carbon tax altogether.



“I bought my first truck aged 22.

“I’ve done nothing else all my life.

“We’re barely surviving.

“Rising fuel costs will mean higher prices on the shelves.

“This affects everyone.”



Yesterday Ireland’s government survived a confidence vote over its handling of the crisis.

There have been reports in the Irish media that some involved in the demos have far-right sympathies.

Kildare county councillor Tom McDonnell, 63, a builder and fuel campaigner who has been branded with that label, said: “I’m not against immigrants, just illegal immigration.”

The dad-of-eight believes the fuel demos will spread to the UK, adding: “We’ve inspired Britain to protest.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

On the other side of the Irish Sea, FairFuelUK’s Howard Cox insisted: “I have always been against direct action, but I am being bombarded with requests to co-lead protests over the next few weeks.”



Britain, too, may soon be facing gridlock.

News.title: Britain's 120,000-drone deal with Ukraine boosts Volodymyr Zelensky's fight
News.content:
Britain's 120,000-drone deal with Ukraine boosts Volodymyr Zelensky's fight

Defence chiefs have signed off a massive new killer drone deal for the Ukraine frontline to help Volodymyr Zelensky's troops fight back the Kremlin advance

View 5 Images Ukrainer Sting interceptor drone on display in Kyiv (Image: AP)

Britain has signed the biggest-ever drone package for Ukraine to help push back Vladimir Putin’s troops in time for the summer fighting season.

‌



It means a staggering 120,000 drones, including those for over-land surveillance, maritime strike operations and intelligence gathering will be sent to Ukraine.

‌



Russia has often been losing at least 1,000 troops-a -day in brutal frontline fighting and this year for the first time the Kremlin has not been able to keep up with recruitment. It means that for every soldier killed or injured in fighting, often by drone strike, the Kremlin has not always been able to replace him with battle reinforcements.

‌



View 5 Images Defence Secretary John Healey (Image: Getty Images)

At the same time it marks a significant investment fortune being spent on British companies, boosting growth and helping increase defence jobs in the UK. The announcement comes as the Defence Secretary John Healey co-chairs a meeting of the Ukraine Defence Contact Group in Berlin.

‌



The MoD said: “The new package, the largest of its kind ever supplied by the UK, will include thousands of long-range strike drones, intelligence and reconnaissance drones, logistics drones and maritime capabilities, which are all battle-proven on Ukraine’s frontline. Deliveries of these new drones to Ukraine have already started this month.'

View 5 Images Devastating Russian attack on Odesa (Image: Odesa OVA/e2w)

‌



Israeli spies persuaded Donald Trump to ignore US intelligence and go to war READ MORE :

‘Drones are proving critical to both Ukrainian counterattacks across the frontline over the past months, as well as their defence against continued Russian attacks. Approximately 6,500 one-way attack drones were launched by Russia against Ukraine in March 2026, a significant increase on February’s total.”

Healey travelled to Berlin to help head the 34th meeting of the 50-nation strong Ukraine Defence Contact Group in Berlin, alongside German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius, Ukrainian Minister of Defence Mykhailo Fedorov, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Most of the investment will be spent with UK-based companies, including Tekever, Windracers and Malloy Aeronautics - creating new UK jobs whilst defending Ukraine’s security and sovereignty.

View 5 Images Zelensky looks at German-Ukraine drones (Image: Action Press/Shutterstock)

‌



The British drone sector is rapidly advancing, and supports both UK security and wider European deterrence, while driving skills and innovation in every region of the UK. Defence Secretary John Healey MP said:

“In the fifth year of Putin's brutal war, the UK is stepping up further and providing the highest ever number of drones for Ukraine this year. This big boost of battle-proven drones will give Ukrainian forces the capability they need to defend their people and fight back against Russian aggression.'

View 5 Images Drone hunter intercepts drone duyring drills, Kyiv (Image: AP)

Article continues below

“With eyes on the Middle East in recent weeks, Putin wants us to be distracted, but Ukrainians continue to fight with huge courage and nothing will distract us from continuing to stand with them for as long as it takes to secure peace.' The new drone package is backed by the UK’s wider £3 billion military support for Ukraine this year, as well as ERA funding.

The Defence Secretary will also confirm that the UK will be providing hundreds of thousands of artillery rounds and thousands of air defence missiles for Ukraine this year.

News.title: US blockade of Strait of Hormuz explained as peace talks fall apart
News.content:
US blockade of Strait of Hormuz explained as peace talks fall apart

Tehran effectively shut down the waterway between Iran and Oman — through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil supply normally passes — following the February 28 attacks by Israel and the US

View 5 Images Donald Trump announced a US blockade on the Strait of Hormuz (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Donald Trump hit back at Iran, after peace talks completely fell apart, by announcing his own Strait of Hormuz blockade.

‌



Tehran effectively shut off the waterway between Iran and Oman, that typically sees a fifth of the world's oil supply pass through, after February 28 when Israel and the US launched attacks on the regime. Iran hit tankers and threatened any vessels that attempted to pass through, bringing the busy waterway to a standstill and plunging the global economy into chaos.

‌



When the US and Iran announced a fragile two-week ceasefire last week, both nations proposed a huge toll for vessels passing through. Peace talks have broken down and the situation with the Strait of Hormuz has become even more contentious.

‌



View 5 Images A ship seen off the coast of Ras al-Khaimahm, in the UAE, on Monday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Fresh warning as Middle East meltdown set to hit high street stores hard READ MORE :

Trump raged on the internet after JD Vance came back from negotiations, on Saturday, in Islamabad, Pakistan, empty handed.

In a fiery Truth Social post on Sunday, The US President said: "I have instructed our navy to seek and interdict every vessel in international waters that has paid a toll to Iran. No one who pays and illegal toll will have safe passage on the high seas. We will also begin destroying mines the Iranians laid in the Straits. Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!"

‌



View 5 Images JD Vance smiling as he boards Air Force Two in Islamabad despite failing to land a peace deal with Iran, on Sunday (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Where is the US blockade?

The blockade started at 3pm BST on Monday which was due to block vessels going into Iranian ports and giving neutral ships a grace period to exit.

It is not clear exactly where the US Navy has been deployed so it is not known exactly where the US could attempt to intercept vessels. The Strait of Hormuz is sandwiched by the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

‌



The US could focus on the Gulf of Oman where a huge amount of the world's oil supply passes. US Central Command (CENTCOM) said more than 12 warships and over 100 fighters are part of the blockade.

View 5 Images Oil tankers and cargo ships lining up in the Strait of Hormuz, on Saturday (Image: AP)

Who will be targeted by the blockade?

The US could focus on Iran's illicit shadow fleet - vessels that use deceptive tactics to move items illegally or that are sanctioned. For example, ships can operate under "flags of convenience", where a flag can be bought from a country with no ties and used to avoid detection.

‌



CENTCOM said the blockade will not "impede freedom of navigation" for ships passing the strait to and from other ports.

The US military said: "The blockade will be enforced impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas, including all Iranian ports on the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman."

CENTCOM added that it would allowed humanitarian vessels, holding items like food and medical supplies, to pass subject to inspection.

‌



View 5 Images Trump's threat to 'eliminate' Iranian ships

How will it be enforced?

The US Navy and government have remained tight-lipped on how it will enforce this blockade. In the past, US forces have used helicopters to get onto tankers accused of operating illegally in the Caribbean.

Nations can also exercise their right to "visit and search", during times of war, and stop or allow vessels to pass, James Kraska, a professor of international maritime law, told The New York Times.

Article continues below

Enforcing this blockade could be complicated and "high-risk", Andreas Krieg, senior lecturer at King's College London's School of Security Studies, told NBC News. He said: "Practically, this would look less like a clean historical blockade and more like a messy, high-risk interdiction regime."

News.title: Major European airline cancels hundreds of flights as UK airports impacted
News.content:
Major European airline cancels hundreds of flights as UK airports impacted

Further strike action has been announced across one of Europe's biggest airline groups, with Lufthansa flight cancellations expected to also impact British passengers

View 2 Images British passengers look set to be caught up in more flight disruption (stock) (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Fresh disruption is looming for British travellers as a new wave of pilot strikes hits one of Europe's biggest airline groups.

‌



Holiday plans have already been thrown into chaos this week after a two-day walkout at Lufthansa forced hundreds of cancellations across Europe, with several UK airports caught in the fallout.

‌



Now, the pilots' union Vereinigung Cockpit (VC) has confirmed further strike action across the airline and its subsidiaries - including Lufthansa Cargo, Lufthansa CityLine and Eurowings.

‌



The walkout is due to begin at 12:01am on April 16 and run until 11:59pm on April 17, with departures from German airports set to bear the brunt - routes to the UK look set to be hit.

The union said flights to several Middle Eastern countries would be exempt due to ongoing tensions in the region, including routes to Egypt, Israel and the UAE.

View 2 Images Fresh walkouts are set to begin on Thursday (stock) (Image: ANNA SZILAGYI/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



The message read: "Due to the current situation in the Middle East, flights operated by Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Lufthansa CityLine from Germany to the following destinations remain exempt from the strike: Azerbaijan, Egypt, Bahrain, Iraq, Israel, Yemen, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates".

Union president Andreas Pinheiro warned the dispute had come to a standstill. "The situation is deadlocked," he said, adding there has been "absolutely no movement" from employers on pensions or pay agreements across the group's airlines.

"Neither Lufthansa and Lufthansa Cargo have made an offer regarding company pension schemes, nor has Lufthansa CityLine made a viable offer for a new collective bargaining agreement on remuneration, nor has Eurowings made any offer regarding company pension schemes," Pinheiro said. "We are not concerned with power struggles or egoism, but with sustainable solutions".

‌



A message on the VC's website read: "Should the employers accept the mediation proposal, the Cockpit Association will promptly submit suggestions for a suitable mediator."

The row has seen more than 1,000 flights cancelled so far, with more than 4,500 UK passengers caught up in the disruption.

Multiple flights travelling to Frankfurt or Munich from London Heathrow, Manchester, Birmingham, and Edinburgh were scrapped today. Lufthansa said only around one-third of their short-haul schedule will be running as normal, while half of its long-haul flights will be cancelled.

Article continues below

Eurowings - which has seen 570 flight cancellations at Frankfurt Airport affecting more than 50,000 travellers - will operate 60 per cent of its schedule.

The strike has seen around 720 flight cancellations at Munich Airport over the last two days.

News.title: UK snow maps reveal 27 cities face April blizzard within days – see full list
News.content:
UK snow maps reveal 27 cities face April blizzard within days – see full list

Snow could impact as many as 27 cities in the UK later this month including Birmingham, Manchester and Edinburgh, according to advanced weather forecasting maps

View 5 Images Major cities could see snow later this month, according to the latest weather maps (Image: WXCharts)

Weather forecasting maps suggest as many as 27 cities across the UK could soon see snow this month.

‌



The GFS weather model shows flurries first falling in the Midlands, the north-west of England and northern parts of Scotland at around 6am on April 26. Birmingham is among the cities that could see some flakes during the initial cold blast.

‌



By 9am, the maps show snow spreading quite widely across the UK, impacting regions just north of London as well as in Wales, Northern Ireland and the far north of Scotland. Parts of Yorkshire could also see snow around this time.

‌



View 5 Images Maps show snow (in purple) falling at 6am on April 26 (Image: WXCharts)

UK weather maps turn icy blue as -4C Arctic blast hits parts of the country READ MORE :

UK weather maps turn yellow as 21C 'mini-heatwave' heads for Britain READ MORE :

Maps for around midday on April 26 show snow falling right across the north of England, the Midlands, a huge chunk of Wales and most of Scotland. Liverpool and Manchester are expected to be in the firing line around this time.

And on April 27 at around 9am, maps show almost all of Wales engulfed in snow, while the heaviest flurries are expected in the far north of Scotland and northern England. In total, the maps suggest 27 cities could see snow during this period.

‌



View 5 Images Snow is expected to spread across the UK by 9am on April 26 (Image: WXCharts)

Glasgow

Edinburgh

Newry

View 5 Images Snow could impact several major cities at around midday on April 26 (Image: WXCharts)

‌



Luckily, the data suggests snow accumulations won’t be greater than 1cm in most of the country. In fact, significant snow is only expected in the Scottish hills where six inches is on the cards.

The Met Office expects temperatures to generally be on the warm side later this month. However, the national weather agency also says "unsettled" conditions are on the cards.

View 5 Images Further snow is on the cards on the morning of April 27 (Image: WXCharts)

Article continues below

The Met Office forecast for April 19 to 28 states: "A few showers around at the start of the period, mainly affecting the far northeast of the UK. For many though Sunday should be fine and dry with spells of warm sunshine.

"Into the following week fronts associated with another Atlantic low will try to push into the UK, but may struggle to make inroads against an area of high pressure to the northeast and are likely to be held at bay.

"So for much of next week plenty of dry weather with sunny spells. Some east coasts could be on the chilly side, but further west temperatures likely feeling quite warm. Toward next weekend and beyond likely turning more unsettled with a return of some rain or showers for many."

News.title: Queen Camilla WILL meet domestic abuse survivors during US tour but NOT Epstein victims
News.content:
Queen Camilla WILL meet domestic abuse survivors during US tour but NOT Epstein victims

The Queen has scheduled several events to meet domestic abuse survivors, but has been advised not to meet victims of sex offender Jeffrey Epstein due to the risk of prejudicing ongoing police probes

View 5 Images Queen Camilla has long advocated for domestic abuse victims and hopes to meet survivors in the United States (Image: ITV)

The Queen will meet domestic abuse survivors on several occasions during the King and Queen's tour of the US, but the royals still will not meet any of Jeffrey Epstein's victims.

‌



The royals have been called upon to meet with sex trafficking victims of the late convicted sex offender, but have been advised to decline due to ongoing police investigations.

‌



The former prince Andrew has constantly been urged to speak to US investigators probing Epstein’s crimes and alongside his ex-wife Sarah Ferguson, was named numerous times in documents released by the US State Department this year referring to the late billionaire financier.

‌



Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna, who co-sponsored a law that compelled the US justice department to release the Epstein files last year, wrote to the King asking him to privately meet victims to hear from them directly about “how powerful individuals and institutions failed them”.

Both the King and Queen have previously expressed how their "sympathies have been, and remain with, the victims of any and all forms of abuse".

The Queen has had a long history of supporting victims of abuse, including featuring in a landmark documentary by Love Monday Productions for ITV in 2004, highlighting the plight of survivors.

‌



View 5 Images Queen Camilla has long advocated for domestic abuse victims and hopes to meet survivors in the United States (Image: Getty Images)

After being stripped of his titles and honours by the King, his brother Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested in February on allegations of misconduct in a public office, relating to allegations he passed on sensitive information to Epstein in his role as a trade envoy for the government.

Buckingham Palace has stated that it would not be possible during this State Visit for a meeting to take place of the kind that has been suggested.

‌



A spokesman said: “We fully understand and appreciate the survivors’ position, but can only reiterate that our position is clear that anything that could potentially impact on ongoing police inquiries and assessments and any potential criminal action that could result from that would be to the detriment of the survivors themselves in their pursuit of justice.”

Charles and Camilla will visit the US from April 27-30, starting in Washington before traveling to New York and Virginia.

The aim of the trip is to strengthen ties between the two nations, and cement the s0-called ‘Special Relationship’, that has been under immense strain after the United States launched war against Iran in the Middle East.

‌



The upcoming trip has been criticised for going ahead in light of the ongoing war in the Middle East waged by President Trump causing global chaos.

Yet President Trump has labelled King Charles "a gentleman" and said he is very much looking forward to welcoming him to the US, after the King hosted the US leader on for an unprecedented second State Visit in Windsor last September.

View 5 Images President Trump has called King Charles a "gentleman" and said he's looking forward to welcoming him to America (Image: AP)

‌



Liberal Democrat Leader Ed Davey even called on the Prime Minister to cancel the King's scheduled state visit, saying: “Keir Starmer should advise the King that the state visit to the US scheduled for April should be called off. At a time when Trump has launched an illegal war that is devastating the Middle East and pushing up energy bills for British families, it’s clear this visit should not go ahead.

“A state visit from our King would be seen as yet another huge diplomatic coup for President Trump, so it should not be given to someone who repeatedly insults and damages our country.”

In response Sir Keir Starmer said: “Mature alliances are not about pretending differences don’t exist. They’re about addressing them directly, respectfully and with a focus on results.”

‌



Palace sources suggested that the King and Queen have a unique role to play in terms of building alliances, even in challenging circumstances, which is a part of the historic strategic objective of State Visits.

A spokesperson for the Foreign Office said: “We are close allies, we do disagree on things, but that doesn’t detract from the value that both sides get from this relationship and have done over many decades.”

But the royals hope the visit will be a cause for partnership and celebration, as well as marking the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, Buckingham Palace said “the visit will be an opportunity to recognise the shared history of our two nations; the breadth of the economic, security and cultural relationship that has developed since then; and the deep people-to-people connections which unite communities.”

‌



As part of the tour the royals will also attend a traditional American Block Party, a public celebration, usually organised by neighbours, where a city street or residential block is closed to traffic.

The party in Virginia will see locals coming out to meet the royals and celebrating America’s 250th birthday.

On the first day of the visit, the King and Queen will be welcomed in Washington informally by President Trump and the First Lady.

‌



They will then attend a private tea and a Garden Party, before being welcomed to the US with a formal ceremony later in the programme at the White House, which will feature a ceremonial military review and a State Dinner in the evening.

View 5 Images King Charles III and US President Donald Trump with Queen Camilla and First Lady Melania Trump at the state banquet at Windsor Castle, Berkshire, on day one of the president's second state visit to the UK on September 17, 2025 in Windsor.

On Tuesday 28, the King will address Congress, only the second time a British Monarch has addressed a joint meeting, following Queen Elizabeth II’s speech at the Capitol during a State Visit to the United States, in 1991.

‌



In New York on Wednesday, April 29, Charles and Camilla will visit the 9/11 memorial, In recognition of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks later this year, as we’ll as a visit to Harlem in the city.

In Virginia, the King and Queen will attend a traditional American Block Party - public celebration, usually organised by neighbours, where a city street or residential block is closed to traffic.

View 5 Images The King and Queen are expected to pay their respects at the 9/11 memorial in New York city, ahead of the 25th anniversary of the attacks later this year (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

After the US visit the Queen will return to the UK while the King will travel to Bermuda, from May 1-2, marking his first visit as Sovereign to a British Overseas Territory.

The King will view a museum exhibition dedicated to the history of Bermuda, furthering his understanding of its connection to the Transatlantic Slave Trade.

The King will also meet representatives from the UK Space Agency to hear about plans to install a new telescope site in Bermuda as part of global efforts to track space debris, supporting international space sustainability.

News.title: Boy thrown from Tate Modern balcony takes 'sad step backward' in recovery
News.content:
Boy thrown from Tate Modern balcony takes 'sad step backward' in recovery

The family of the boy thrown from a balcony at the Tate Modern art gallery in London by Jonty Bravery have shared a heartbreaking update about his ongoing rehabilitation after surgery

View 3 Images Tate Modern pictured on the day of the lockdown and evacuation after the incident (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The family of a boy who was hurled from the 10th-floor balcony of the Tate Modern art gallery have revealed that his recovery appears to have taken a "sad step backward".

‌



The French youngster was just six years old when he was seriously injured in an attack carried out by then-teenager Jonty Bravery at the London landmark in August 2019. The French child, who was visiting with his parents on holiday, survived a 100 foot (30 metre) plunge but was left with life-altering injuries, including a brain bleed and numerous broken bones.

‌



His family, who affectionately refer to him as "notre petit chevalier" – our little knight – shared an update on a GoFundMe page on Tuesday, revealing that the youngster's rehabilitation is "proving longer and more difficult than expected" following an operation in January.

‌



They said: "He is still hospitalised in a rehabilitation centre because he is still unable to walk. He has only been able to have weekend leave for the past three weeks, in a wheelchair, which frustrates him greatly: it feels like a sad step backward."

View 3 Images Jonty Bravery admitted attempted murder (Image: PA)

In their previous update in October, the family described how the boy had reached his "long set" goal of being able to run, jump and swim once more.

‌



"He is eager to be able to walk again and resume a normal life outside the rehabilitation centre, even if this normal life means spending half his time in treatment and only the other half at school," they continued in their latest post. The family revealed he is particularly eager to leave hospital as they have "finally" discovered a school "perfectly suited to his needs", which he was able to visit before his operation.

The post added: "In a very short time, he made new friends who have stayed in touch despite his extended absence. They encourage him and eagerly await his return. It's a warm welcome he hasn't received at school in a long time."

View 3 Images An artist's impression depicts Bravery in court (Image: Julia Quenzler / SWNS)

‌



The family explained that they remain uncertain how much longer his hospital stay will need to continue, stating: "Our little knight, as courageous as ever, continues to fight and train, and we will remain by his side to support him no matter what."

London nurse Vicky Diplacto, whose brother was paralysed following an accident abroad, established the GoFundMe appeal to assist. Bravery, now 24, was living in supported accommodation when the attack occurred but was permitted out without supervision.

He had planned to choose and kill someone, a court subsequently heard. Bravery, who was 17 at the time, admitted attempted murder and received a life sentence with a minimum term of 15 years.

Article continues below

He returned to court earlier this year, when he was jailed for 16 weeks after being found guilty of assaulting two nurses at Broadmoor, a high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire, in September 2024. In 2020, he received a 14-week jail sentence after admitting to attacking staff at the same hospital.

News.title: Putin allies confess love for Donald Trump but 'fear he will launch nuke strike'
News.content:
Putin allies confess love for Donald Trump but 'fear he will launch nuke strike'

Russian state TV host Vladimir Solovyov said he likes Donald Trump 'a lot' as he is 'destroying NATO' - but warned the US president could launch a nuclear strike

Vladimir Solovyov says he likes Trump for 'destroying NATO'

Putin's cronies have praised Donald Trump on Russian state TV - with one admitting "I like him a lot" while at the same time warning his behaviour could push the world closer to a nuclear war.

‌



The remarks came during an exchange on the prime-time programme Sunday Evening with Vladimir Solovyov, who appeared alongside Director General of Mosfilm Karen Shakhnazarov and State Duma member Semyon Bagdasarov.

‌



The TV host led the praise for Trump but suggested the US president's unpredictability made nuclear escalation impossible to rule out. "No one can guarantee that America won't carry out a nuclear strike against Iran," he said.

‌



View 3 Images Solovyov told the panel he likes Trump 'a lot' (Image: Russian Media Monitor/Youtube)

"I like him, I like Trump a lot," Solovyov told the panel. "He is destroying NATO. It's a harsh version of an American 'perestroyka' (restructuring)."

He added: "He won't calm down until he destroys America, all of his allies and all of his alliances. Trump suddenly realised that weapons are coming to Iran from someplace."

‌



View 3 Images Putin pictured with Vladimir Solovyov (R) who said he likes Trump 'a lot' (Image: Getty Images)

Solovyov's comments came after Bagdasarov warned political turmoil in Israel had pushed the country into a "dead end", arguing the situation was so volatile that talk of a possible nuclear strike against Iran could not be dismissed. "No one can guarantee it won't happen," he said.

Solovyov questioned whether the same nuclear risk could apply to the US under Trump, before insisting he "likes Trump a lot".

‌



View 3 Images The panel warned Trump could launch a nuclear strike against Iran (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Bagdasarov took a harsher line, describing Trump as a "crackpot" and saying "God only knows what's going on in his head", while arguing Israel was more likely than any other power to escalate towards nuclear action.

Last month, Soloyov warned of an "end times" nuclear war sparked by ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

Article continues below

"With what is happening in America it is clear that nuclear weapons will be used," Solovyov told guests on his show. "Trump is already talking about it openly. I've been talking about it for several years. If we keep thinking 'No, it isn't possible,' it won't help us.

"The scariest thing that will happen is that Trump will use nuclear weapons and understand that this is not a cure-all," he added. "The size of Iran as a country is such that regardless of what kind of nuclear weapons you use… afterwards Iran would respond and the last restriction will fall."

News.title: Tragedy as mum Claire Boland who made desperate 'last resort' plea five months ago dies
News.content:
Tragedy as mum Claire Boland who made desperate 'last resort' plea five months ago dies

Claire Boland, from Stockport, Greater Manchester, had been waiting more than five years for a kidney transplant due to her rare blood combination - and the situation became dire last year

View 3 Images Claire Boland has died after suffering a bleed on the brain (Image: Claire Boland)

A courageous mother who waited more than five years for a kidney donor has tragically passed away.

Claire Boland, from Stockport, Greater Manchester, suffered a "catastrophic" bleed on the brain before losing her life on Saturday April 4. She said last year she had "lost all hope" in the find a suitable match for a kidney, as her rare blood type meant her chances were two in every 10,000 people.

Friends, family and loved ones all came forward to be tested, yet none proved compatible. She suffered a brain bleed while out at bingo with her mum and best friend. It has not yet been confirmed whether the bleed on Claire's brain and her previous health complications are connected.

She leaves behind her husband Damien, daughters Ileana, two, and Elodie, 13, along with her wider family, reports the Manchester Evening News.

Major organ donor development headed by team that saved Mirror boy Max Johnson READ MORE :

View 3 Images Claire, husband Damien, and their children, two-year-old Ileana and 12-year-old Elodie (Image: Claire Boland)

Claire made a desperate public appeal for a donor just five months ago. She was first diagnosed with type one diabetes at just eight years old, which led to a childhood spent in and out of hospital for 'weeks on end'.

Around seven years ago, she developed kidney failure that 'quickly became end-stage'. Claire endured gruelling sessions of haemodialysis, monthly iron transfusions and frequent visits to the doctor for high blood pressure — all on top of managing her diabetes. "It's the not knowing that's so affecting." Claire said in November. "It's such a strain on my mental health... my marriage, my children. I spend my days going to and from the hospital for all sorts of different appointments. I don't feel like I have a life anymore. My life is dialysis."

A desperate Claire admitted: "Putting out this call is my last resort. I feel like it's all on me now to find a donor because I'm just having no luck with the transplant and living donor lists. I don't have any hope anymore. I'm just pleading with people to come forward and get tested."

Heartbreakingly, a matching donor was never found. Claire's mum Deborah Kershaw recalled: "We went to bingo on March 29 and everything was fine... she was fine. We got a drink and sat down. She was just chatting and laughing with her friend.

"She then went to order some food, came back, and the bingo started. I think they'd literally shouted about two numbers and she just sort of flinched and shouted 'mum, I've got a really bad headache'. She was scrunching her eyes up and she kept sort of falling forward.

"Then I noticed her face had started to droop a little bit, so I said 'come on, we need to get you home'." Claire subsequently lost all movement in one leg and her left arm, and when she attempted to get to her feet, she collapsed to the ground. Deborah: "The bingo hall manager ran over and we rang 999. They came straight away and we actually knew one of the paramedics because he'd dealt with Claire before on numerous occasions when she'd had funny turns.

"So they got her sorted, got her into the ambulance and rushed us straight to Stepping Hill Hospital. They thought she'd had a stroke. She was still complaining of horrendous pain in her head, just saying it was really hurting, asking for painkillers. Then she started projectile vomiting."

View 3 Images Claire is pictured with her husband Damien (Image: Claire Boland)

A scan revealed a 'quick, catastrophic bleed to the back of her brain'. Doctors explained they were unable to intervene due to the location and extent of the bleeding.

"If they [had have] transferred her to Salford and operated, she would have passed away on the table. If she did survive the operation, they said she would have been completely brain damaged and she wouldn't have been our Claire anymore.

"So she was on a ventilator, keeping her going. She was heavily sedated." Sedation and ventilation were withdrawn on 31 March. Claire continued fighting for four more days.

Deborah said: "Claire being the fighter she is, she fought for another four days and she sadly passed on April 4. It was very traumatic. Just very sudden. You know, everything she's been through, and yet she managed to get through all that, and then it's a bleed on the brain." Claire's family has launched a GoFundMe page to help cover her funeral expenses and support Damien and their daughters.

What Kidney Donors Need to Know: Before, During and After Donation

Deborah said: "Claire didn't have any life insurance due to her illnesses, so it's all been a bit of a struggle." Honouring her daughter's memory, she added: Claire was lovely. She was absolutely amazing. She was always smiling despite her issues. She didn't let anything get her down.

"She had a heart of gold and would do anything for anybody. She always put other people before herself and she lived for her family - her husband and her girls.

"Her main goal was to go on holiday with the girls. Because of dialysis she wasn't allowed to go abroad, so she desperately wanted a transplant so she could take her daughters away and have a normal life with them.

‌



"She was always happy. She didn't let anything get her down. She'd ring me and have a moan like we all do, but she just kept going, kept smiling, kept fighting. She was a true fighter. It's completely destroyed us. She was my rock. She was my world.

"Her brothers and sister are absolutely devastated. They've lost their oldest sister. It's just hard - you don't expect it. You go for a game of bingo and someone ends up losing their life.

"We're just trying to rally around Damien and help with the children with school holidays and things like that. We all work full-time, so we''e trying to arrange who can take time off and help out. We just want to get as much support as we can for Damien and the girls."

A government ethics group has claimed President Donald Trump’s store has branded more than 600 new items during his second term to “profit off the presidency.”

Trump and his supporters are known for donning red “MAGA” hats, but there is a slew of other merchandise that fans can get their hands on. Typically, people score merchandise from their favorite musicians at concert venues, but now they are getting the latest “Trump 2028” T-shirt from their favorite politician, courtesy of the Trump Store.

The Trump Store is the official retail website of the Trump Organization, which is currently run by the president’s two eldest sons, Donald Jr. and Eric.

The nonprofit organization Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, also known as CREW, reported Tuesday that in the first 14 months of Trump’s second term as president, the Trump Store has sold at least 622 new products, costing a total of nearly $43,000.

open image in gallery A government ethics group has claimed President Donald Trump’s store has branded more than 600 new items during his second term to 'profit off the presidency' ( AFP via Getty Images )

“This is an unprecedented level of monetization of the presidency, even by the standards of Trump’s own first term,” the ethics group said.

The White House has denied claims that Trump has profited from his time in office.

The Trump Store launched in 2017, early in Trump’s first presidential term, according to CREW.

The store brought in a whopping $8.8 million in 2024, which was the year Trump was elected president for the second time, CREW reported, citing Trump’s last published financial records.

open image in gallery The Trump Store reportedly brought in a whopping $8.8 million in 2024 ( AFP via Getty Images )

Last August, The New Yorker reported that Trump and his family had made an estimated $3.4 billion, so far, off his two presidential terms.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt told The Independent at the time, “ The claims that this President has profited from his time in office are absolutely absurd — in comparison to what he could have made if he didn’t have to deal with the fake news and corrupt political opponents, the President has lost hundreds of millions of dollars to serve this country.”

When reached for comment on CREW’s reporting Tuesday, the White House referenced Leavitt’s previous comment denouncing claims that Trump is profiting from the presidency.

“President Trump has always practiced integrity and transparency, which is why he is and has been forthcoming in sharing his financial disclosures,” Leavitt’s statement said.

open image in gallery The Trump Store is probably best known for selling hats, including the 'Trump was right about everything' cap that former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene wore to Trump’s address to Congress in 2025 before she had a public falling out with the president ( Getty Images )

The Independent has reached out to the Trump Organization for comment.

The Trump Store is probably best known for selling hats, including the “USA” cap that the president has been photographed wearing and the “Trump was right about everything” cap that former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene wore to Trump’s address to Congress in 2025 before she had a public falling out with the president.

The store also sells T-shirts, including one with a print of Trump’s 2023 Fulton County mugshot with the word “Daddy,” and pretty much any other item you can think of, such as a single pastel Trump pickleball paddle for $180 and Trump coffee pods for a more reasonably priced $18.

open image in gallery Probably the most problematic products sold on the Trump Store website are the 'Trump 2028' hats, T-shirts and beer koozies ( Getty Images )

Probably the most problematic items sold on the Trump Store’s website are the “Trump 2028” hats, T-shirts and beer koozies.

The president has entertained the idea of an unconstitutional third term, telling reporters on Air Force One last October, “I would love to do it.”

The Trump Store is but one of several businesses the Trump family is involved in, including a crypto venture called World Liberty Financial and Trump Media and Technology Group, which owns Truth Social.
